items.label: Remove viruses
items.why: Run a portable, on-demand malware scan without replacing the client’s existing protection.
items.boundary: Contain spreading compromise first; download a fresh copy for the job and treat a clean scan as limited evidence.
items.freeUse: Free Microsoft download
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents malware detection/removal, a detailed scan log and a 10-day download expiry; this is a workflow-based pick, not a comparative cleanup rating.
items.firstStep: Disconnect a suspected compromised PC from the network before scanning; use the incident guide if encryption is spreading.
quickSteps: Record the symptoms and isolate affected connections; keep the existing real-time protection in place.
On a trusted PC, download a fresh Microsoft Safety Scanner; transfer it safely and run a Full scan.
Save the scan log, review remaining symptoms and persistence, then follow the guide’s cleanup or rebuild decision.

items.label: Fix a printer
items.why: Use the supported Windows printer diagnostic to separate connection, queue and device problems.
items.boundary: Scope changes to the affected printer; preserve unrelated queued jobs and use a driver suitable for the PC architecture.
items.freeUse: Included with supported Windows
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft routes Windows 11 printing problems through its printer troubleshooter and provides device, connection and test-page checks.
items.firstStep: Check that the intended printer is powered on, ready and connected before changing its queue or driver.
quickSteps: Check paper, ink or toner, displayed errors and the selected printer; compare a device test page if available.
Run the printer troubleshooter in Windows Get Help on the affected PC and review the exact queue or connection finding.
Apply the indicated repair, then print a test page and the user’s original document.

items.label: Fix internet
items.why: Start with supported connection diagnostics before escalating to packet capture or network resets.
items.boundary: A shared outage needs the network owner; retain VPN and adapter settings before disruptive changes.
items.freeUse: Included with supported Windows
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents a Network and Internet diagnostic and an ordered set of Wi-Fi, router and device comparisons.
items.firstStep: Check whether one device, one connection or the whole office has lost access.
quickSteps: Check the cable or Wi-Fi connection and compare another device on the same network.
In Windows Get Help, search “connect to network and internet” and run network diagnostics.
Follow the relevant address, gateway or DNS branch, then retest the original site and business service.

items.label: Fix email
items.why: Use the mail client and service scope to choose the correct authentication, startup or connectivity repair.
items.boundary: The classic Outlook diagnostics do not apply to new Outlook; do not delete a profile before protecting local-only data.
items.freeUse: Diagnostics are included; email service licensing is separate
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft identifies separate classic Outlook diagnostics and explicitly excludes new Outlook from those tests.
items.firstStep: Check webmail and identify whether the affected app is classic Outlook or new Outlook before changing a profile.
quickSteps: Test sign-in and send/receive in webmail; record the exact error and whether other users are affected.
For classic Outlook, run the matching Windows Get Help diagnostic; for new Outlook, use its supported troubleshooting branch.
Retest send, receive and the affected shared mailbox or calendar; preserve local-only mail before any profile rebuild.

items.label: Recover a failing drive
items.why: Preserve readable data in an image with a resumable mapfile before attempting file-system repairs.
items.boundary: Confirm source and destination; stop for physical damage, repeated disconnects or irreplaceable data that warrants a recovery specialist.
items.freeUse: Free software; destination storage is separate
items.qualityBasis: The GNU manual explains good-area-first recovery, resumable mapfiles and unreadable-range accounting; an image alone does not prove usable files. SystemRescue provides a ready-to-boot ISO containing GNU ddrescue; imaging remains an operator-led task.
items.firstStep: Stop using the source disk; clicking, physical damage or irreplaceable data needs a recovery-specialist decision first.
quickSteps: Boot a separate SystemRescue USB and identify source and destination by model, serial and size.
Follow the GNU ddrescue imaging procedure with a persistent mapfile; do not run file-system repairs on the source.
Work on an image copy, record unreadable ranges and open the client’s priority files to verify recovery.

items.label: Recover deleted files
items.why: Recover recognizable file contents from healthy media or an image when an intact backup cannot restore them.
items.boundary: Stop source-disk writes and recover to another disk; original names and folders may be lost, and failing media needs imaging first.
items.freeUse: Free and open source for business use
items.qualityBasis: The project documents read-only source access and recovery by file signatures across damaged file systems; recoverability still depends on surviving data.
items.firstStep: Stop writing to the affected disk and check the backup or recycle bin before attempting recovery.
quickSteps: Use healthy media or a preserved image; route an unstable drive to image-first recovery.
Run PhotoRec against that source and send recovered output to a different disk.
Open representative recovered files and record missing items; retain the source until acceptance.

items.label: Fix a slow PC
items.why: Inspect process activity and startup entries to identify a concrete cause before changing settings.
items.boundary: Choose utilities supported on the client’s Windows release; observe before terminating processes or disabling startup entries.
items.freeUse: Free Microsoft utilities
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents process ownership, handles, loaded modules and startup inspection; these observations support a measured troubleshooting decision.
items.firstStep: Reproduce one slow task and check storage health before applying cleanup or startup changes.
quickSteps: Use Process Explorer to identify the CPU, memory or I/O bottleneck during that task.
Inspect the relevant process or startup entry with Microsoft Sysinternals Suite and make one justified change.
Repeat the same task and compare its duration, resource use and responsiveness.

items.label: Help remotely
items.why: Start a one-time attended Windows support session with separate screen-sharing and control approval.
items.boundary: Requires internet and a present user; use the organization’s approved managed tool when unattended access or session audit logs are required.
items.freeUse: Free Microsoft app; organization policy applies
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft’s IT guidance documents the session-code flow, helper sign-in, user approval and the absence of local session logs.
items.firstStep: Confirm the user and support technician through the existing support channel before sharing a session code.
quickSteps: Open Microsoft Quick Assist on both Windows PCs; the helper signs in and supplies the temporary code.
Have the user approve screen sharing and any separately requested control before making the agreed change.
Test the original task with the user, end the session and record the work in the service ticket.

items.label: Fix Windows updates
items.why: Use Microsoft’s supported update diagnostic before manual component resets.
items.boundary: Follow organizational update policy; route storage or component-store damage to the relevant guide.
items.freeUse: Included with supported Windows
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft recommends the Windows Update troubleshooter, then a restart and a fresh update check.
items.firstStep: Record the failing update or KB number, error code and pending restart before retrying it.
quickSteps: Confirm free space, a stable connection and a planned restart window.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter in Windows Get Help and review its findings.
Restart when required, check for updates again and verify the affected update and original task.

items.label: Repair Windows files
items.why: Check and repair the Windows component store before the guide’s system-file verification step.
items.boundary: Check storage health and recovery options first; use the correct online or offline target and a compatible repair source.
items.freeUse: Included with Windows
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents corruption checks, repairable/non-repairable image states and controlled repair sources.
items.firstStep: Confirm storage health, a recovery route and the intended Windows installation before repair writes.
quickSteps: Run the guide’s DISM checks and repair against the correct online or offline installation.
Follow with System File Checker and record whether corruption was repaired or remains unresolved.
Restart if required, repeat the original task and retain the relevant repair logs.

items.label: Fix a PC that will not boot
items.why: Use the built-in recovery environment to distinguish startup repair from data-preserving recovery or reinstall.
items.boundary: Encrypted recovery may require the correct key; do not reset or reinstall before protecting required data.
items.freeUse: Included with licensed Windows
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents the recovery environment, Startup Repair and separate causes of boot failure.
items.firstStep: Record the startup error and confirm disk health and BitLocker recovery access before attempting repairs.
quickSteps: Check power, attached devices and the selected boot disk; stop if storage is failing.
Open Windows Recovery Environment and run Startup Repair for the identified installation when appropriate.
Follow the matching recovery branch, verify a normal boot and open priority files before closing the job.

items.label: Diagnose crashes
items.why: Use crash evidence to select the appropriate hardware or driver test.
items.boundary: Dump analysis is an operator task; a module named in one crash does not by itself prove the root cause.
items.freeUse: Free Microsoft debugger
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents bug-check investigation and WinDbg dump analysis rather than treating every stop error as faulty RAM.
items.firstStep: Record the stop code, failure time and recent hardware or driver changes before replacing components.
quickSteps: Check reliability and event history, available crash dumps and storage health to narrow the failure.
For a dump, use WinDbg to inspect the crash evidence; follow the indicated driver, memory or hardware branch.
Change one supported cause at a time and repeat the failing workload while checking for new crashes.

items.label: Free disk space
items.why: See which folders and file types occupy a healthy disk before choosing a cleanup target.
items.boundary: Avoid scanning failing media; confirm file ownership and a recovery route before deleting anything.
items.freeUse: Free and open source for business use
items.qualityBasis: The official project documents size-sorted lists, file-type statistics and treemaps that make disk allocation inspectable.
items.firstStep: Confirm the disk is healthy and choose the drive to inspect before deleting any files.
quickSteps: Scan that drive with WinDirStat and identify the largest folders and file types.
Confirm ownership and recovery options, then remove only approved files or application-managed caches.
Recheck free space and open the affected application to confirm it still works.

items.label: Clone or move a drive
items.why: Use a graphical bootable imaging tool for planned migration of healthy storage.
items.boundary: Do not clone failing media as a routine migration; smaller destinations need separate planning and may require source resizing.
items.freeUse: Free open-source software; destination storage is separate
items.qualityBasis: Rescuezilla provides a bootable graphical backup/clone environment and documents its smaller-disk limitation.
items.firstStep: Confirm a healthy source, a verified backup and a destination large enough for the selected clone or restore.
quickSteps: Boot Rescuezilla from a separate USB and identify every source and destination by model, serial and size.
Choose the intended clone or image operation; confirm the destination may be overwritten before starting.
Boot the destination alone and verify files, applications, encryption recovery and backup operation.

items.label: Restore a file backup
items.why: Create encrypted file snapshots and restore a representative sample to prove the backup is usable.
items.boundary: This is a file-backup workflow, not a bare-metal image; retain the repository password and test a separate restore target.
items.freeUse: Free software; storage is separate
items.qualityBasis: The official documentation provides repository checks, snapshot selection and explicit restore commands.
items.firstStep: Identify the backup format, snapshot date and recoverable credentials before choosing the restore tool.
quickSteps: For a restic repository, inspect snapshots and run the documented repository checks.
Restore the required snapshot or files to a separate destination using the scoped procedure.
Open representative files, check permissions and record the restored date and any missing data.

items.label: Make a boot USB
items.why: Write a trusted operating-system or rescue image to a USB drive with explicit target and boot-mode choices.
items.boundary: Writing erases the selected USB; verify its identity and use a trusted image that matches the target firmware.
items.freeUse: Free software; image licensing is separate
items.qualityBasis: The official project documents BIOS/UEFI media creation, image checksums and portable operation.
items.firstStep: Choose the official ISO and identify a USB drive that may be erased.
quickSteps: Download the correct image and check its published checksum or signature where supplied.
In Rufus, confirm the USB model and capacity, select the ISO and choose the target’s firmware-compatible options.
Write the USB, check the log and test that it boots before taking it to the client.

items.label: Set up a new PC
items.why: Make approved application setup repeatable while checking the complete workstation handoff.
items.boundary: WinGet does not replace deployment policy, application licensing or migration of user data and settings.
items.freeUse: Free package manager; application licenses are separate
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents package identification, installation and import through WinGet; each package retains its own licensing.
items.firstStep: Confirm the owner, approved applications, identity setup and recovery requirements before installing software.
quickSteps: Complete the approved Windows and device-driver updates and check basic hardware operation.
Use WinGet for approved available packages, reviewing the package identity and each application’s license.
Verify sign-in, encryption recovery, backup and the user’s daily tasks before handoff.

items.label: Maintain a PC
items.why: Review and apply justified updates as part of a measured maintenance visit.
items.boundary: Review package changes individually; a bulk upgrade is not a substitute for compatibility and restart planning.
items.freeUse: Free package manager; application licenses are separate
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents listing and selecting upgrades with WinGet; INTA maintenance adds backup and acceptance checks.
items.firstStep: Agree a maintenance window and confirm the backup can restore files before changing software.
quickSteps: Check storage health, free space, protection status and a representative backup restore.
Review available Windows and application updates; use WinGet only for approved package changes.
Reboot in the agreed window, retest essential tasks and record the versions and remaining issues.

items.label: Start a repair
items.why: Choose the right service path and preserve recoverability before downloading utilities.
items.boundary: Do not provoke repeated failures on damaged storage or continue routine repair during an active incident.
items.freeUse: No extra download needed
items.qualityBasis: The INTA intake procedure records scope, recovery constraints and acceptance evidence; Microsoft documents recovery choices and their consequences.
items.firstStep: Record the exact symptom, affected device and desired result before making changes.
quickSteps: Confirm permission, the last working time and any recent change with the user.
Check for spreading compromise, failing storage and missing recovery access before normal troubleshooting.
Reproduce the problem, record a baseline and choose the matching guide with a clear success test.

items.label: Contain ransomware
items.why: Contain the incident and protect recovery options before routine cleanup.
items.boundary: Coordinate evidence and shutdown decisions with the incident lead; a clean antivirus result is not a release decision.
items.freeUse: No extra download needed for the first response
items.qualityBasis: CISA and Microsoft prioritize isolation, evidence, scope assessment and a coordinated recovery process.
items.firstStep: Isolate affected connections and alert the incident owner immediately if files are being encrypted or compromise is spreading.
quickSteps: Disconnect affected systems from networks and protect reachable backups without destroying useful evidence.
Preserve the timeline, ransom note and available logs privately; scope affected accounts and systems with the incident owner.
Follow the incident plan for credential containment, clean rebuild and verified restoration before reconnecting.

items.label: Recover an office outage
items.why: Restore dependencies in a controlled order instead of installing an unrelated repair utility.
items.boundary: Use the organization’s infrastructure runbook and qualified electrical or hardware support where required.
items.freeUse: No extra download needed for triage
items.qualityBasis: The INTA outage guide supplies the service dependency sequence; Microsoft explains that an unexpected-restart event alone does not identify the cause.
items.firstStep: Confirm safe power and the affected business services, then assign one recovery owner.
quickSteps: Check power, UPS status and network reachability without repeatedly cycling unstable equipment.
Restore dependencies in the guide’s order: network, storage, identity and the affected application services.
Test a real user workflow and backup status, then record the outage timeline and remaining faults.

items.label: Repair domain sign-in
items.why: Test and repair the member computer’s secure channel after connectivity and time are correct.
items.boundary: This member-computer test is not for domain controllers; installing PowerShell 7 or rejoining the domain is not the first step.
items.freeUse: Windows PowerShell 5.1 is already included on the target PC
items.qualityBasis: Microsoft documents secure-channel testing and repair on domain members and warns against using this cmdlet on domain controllers.
items.firstStep: On the affected domain-member PC, check the domain DNS, time and domain-controller reachability first.
quickSteps: Use existing Windows PowerShell 5.1 to run the guide’s diagnostic secure-channel check on the member PC.
Repair only a confirmed trust fault using an authorized account and the scoped procedure.
Verify domain sign-in, a required shared resource and the secure-channel result.

items.label: Troubleshoot with AI
items.why: Use AI to structure hypotheses and explain evidence while the technician owns execution and verification.
items.boundary: Use an approved account and sanitized data; free-plan limits apply and generated instructions can be wrong.
items.freeUse: Free plan available; organization approval and usage limits apply
items.qualityBasis: OpenAI documents free-plan access and data controls; the NIST profile identifies generative-AI risks requiring human evaluation.
items.firstStep: Prepare a redacted error, timeline and environment summary that your organization permits you to share.
quickSteps: Give ChatGPT the observed symptoms and ask for competing causes with one reversible discriminating test.
Check the proposed action against the official documentation and the actual target before running it.
Record the observed result, reject unsupported guesses and confirm the fix with the original task.

items.label: Finish the job and hand over
items.why: Close the service job with proof, clear ownership and recoverable records.
items.boundary: Keep passwords, recovery keys and customer evidence in the approved private record, not this public wiki.
items.freeUse: No extra download needed
items.qualityBasis: The INTA handoff guide and template define outcome verification, access cleanup, private evidence references and ownership.
items.firstStep: Repeat the original user task and collect acceptance evidence before closing the case.
quickSteps: Verify the requested outcome and record any remaining issue or agreed limitation.
Remove temporary access and case-only tools; record changes and private recovery references in the handoff template.
Confirm user acceptance, the next owner and any follow-up date.

items.label: Find a file
items.why: Locate files and folders by name using a local index instead of repeatedly browsing directories.
items.boundary: Scope the desktop index to approved locations; the separate server product has paid business licensing.
items.freeUse: Free desktop edition for business use
items.qualityBasis: The official FAQ documents filename indexing, live updates and NTFS requirements; the published license and developer guidance permit commercial desktop use.
items.firstStep: Search by the known filename or extension in approved local folders.
quickSteps: Open the Everything desktop app and limit indexing to the locations needed for this case.
Search a distinctive part of the name, then check the result’s path and modification time.
Open the correct file and remove any temporary case-only indexing settings.

items.label: Inspect network traffic
items.why: Explain a stubborn DNS or TCP failure with a narrowly scoped packet capture after basic connection checks.
items.boundary: Start with the guide’s address, gateway and DNS checks; capture only authorized traffic and keep case data private.
items.freeUse: Free software; capture-driver terms apply
items.qualityBasis: The official guide documents packet inspection and filtering; the capture-driver publisher confirms the relevant free-use exception.
items.firstStep: Use packet capture only after basic link, address, gateway and DNS checks have narrowed the fault.
quickSteps: Get authorization and choose the smallest interface, host and time window that can reproduce the issue.
Capture the failing request in Wireshark and inspect the relevant DNS or connection exchange.
Apply one evidenced fix, repeat the request and store the capture only in the private case record.

items.label: Test memory
items.why: Test memory outside the running operating system when crash evidence points to RAM or memory stability.
items.boundary: Record firmware settings and test duration; memory errors need isolation, and a passing run does not rule out other crash causes.
items.freeUse: Free and open source for business use
items.qualityBasis: The official project documents independent boot testing, error investigation and supported firmware/platform requirements.
items.firstStep: Use this branch when crash evidence suggests memory instability, after recording firmware and overclock settings.
quickSteps: Create the supported Memtest86+ boot media and preserve recovery keys before any necessary firmware change.
Boot the test, record passes and errors, and isolate modules or slots using the hardware guide.
Retest the corrected configuration and restore the intended firmware settings.

decisions.action: Use the official ISO and Rufus; confirm the selected USB can be erased and choose firmware-compatible options.
decisions.expected: The intended image is written to the correct device.

decisions.symptom: Several verified images must stay on one USB
decisions.action: Use the documented Ventoy install/update path and copy the checked images to its data partition.
decisions.expected: The expected images appear in the boot menu.

decisions.symptom: The publisher supplies a checksum
decisions.action: Run Get-FileHash for the exact downloaded file and compare it with the official value before writing.
decisions.expected: The calculated hash matches the trusted release record.

decisions.symptom: Writing finished but the client may have unusual hardware
decisions.action: Boot-test the intended firmware mode and verify keyboard, storage, network and the required recovery tool.
decisions.expected: The actual service path works on representative hardware rather than only completing an image write.

doneWhen: Image source, hash and release are recorded.

escalateWhen: The target USB or its erase permission is uncertain.

decisions.symptom: The failure has several plausible causes
decisions.action: Provide the sanitized reproduction and ask for ranked causes plus one small test that separates the leading possibilities.
decisions.expected: The output distinguishes observations from assumptions and predicts a test result.

decisions.symptom: The assistant proposes a command
decisions.action: Check the exact target, shell, privileges, writes and rollback against the official product documentation before execution.
decisions.expected: The technician understands and approves the scoped action.

decisions.symptom: A test contradicts the proposed cause
decisions.action: Return the exact sanitized result and require a revised hypothesis rather than repeating an unchanged failed action.
decisions.expected: The next diagnostic follows the new evidence.

decisions.symptom: The repair is ready to document
decisions.action: Draft the cause/change/test note from verified observations, then review it before saving.
decisions.expected: The handoff contains demonstrated facts and explicit remaining uncertainty.

doneWhen: The original task passes a real test independent of the AI answer.
Executed actions match the actual environment and no unnecessary private content was shared.
escalateWhen: The proposed action is destructive, unsupported or lacks a verified target.
The organization has not approved the intended data/account boundary.

preventive-maintenance.goal: Complete a useful health, update and recovery check without disrupting the user’s working setup.
preventive-maintenance.startHere: Agree the maintenance window and identify the user’s current problem. Verify a usable backup before changes.

decisions.symptom: The device has recurring failures or storage warnings
decisions.action: Check Reliability Monitor and drive health; move actual faults to their repair or recovery guide before routine maintenance.
decisions.expected: The maintenance plan is based on observed faults rather than cleanup rituals.

decisions.symptom: Application updates are available
decisions.action: Run winget upgrade to list them, review compatibility and update only the approved packages in the maintenance window.
decisions.expected: The selected versions are installed and any planned restart is completed.

decisions.symptom: A full disk or missing local file is the concern
decisions.action: Use WinDirStat for capacity or Everything for a filename; confirm ownership and retention before deleting or moving anything.
decisions.expected: The relevant path is identified and any approved cleanup has a measured result.

decisions.symptom: Backup jobs report success
decisions.action: Restore a representative item to a separate location and open it with the intended application.
decisions.expected: The backup is demonstrably usable, with its recovery point recorded.

decisions.symptom: Changes are complete
decisions.action: Restart as planned and repeat the user’s main app, network, printing and backup checks.
decisions.expected: Normal work succeeds and all deferred issues have owners.

doneWhen: Protection, hardware health and backup restoration have been checked.
The normal workload works after maintenance and restart.
Each unresolved item has an explicit next action and owner.
escalateWhen: Storage failure or active compromise changes the service route.
An unplanned critical workload would be interrupted.
